## HIGH-priority finding details

### H-1: `/ai-implement` PR comments are handled by the orchestrator's webhook, not `comment-trigger.yml`  (2/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Eleven root pages described `/ai-implement` gap-fill comments as handled entirely inside a synced `comment-trigger.yml` GitHub Actions workflow, never involving the orchestrator, listed `comment-trigger.yml` as a synced file, and understated what `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` gates.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/workflow-sync.ts:27-32` actively **removes** `.github/workflows/comment-trigger.yml` from a target repo on sync. `ai-implement/src/webhook.ts:150-520` shows the orchestrator's `POST /api/github/webhook` handler matching `/ai-implement` comments directly, gated on `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, with no polling fallback for synced repos. `comment-trigger.yml` still exists only for repos that haven't re-synced.
- **Edit**: Removed `comment-trigger.yml` from synced-file lists across setup/quickstart/workflow-templates pages, rewrote the webhook-configuration consequence text in `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` and `setup/github-app.mdx` to state the webhook is required (not optional) for `/ai-implement` on synced repos, rewrote the troubleshooting accordion with the real webhook prerequisites, and added legacy-vs-synced caveats to the Bedrock repo-variable steps.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in both runs.

### H-2: The "gap analysis" PR-comment feature doesn't exist as documented — real feature is `post-push-review`  (2/2 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/gap-analysis.mdx` and mentions across `how-it-works.mdx`, `index.mdx`, `introduction.mdx`, `quickstart.mdx`, `reference/troubleshooting.mdx`, `customize/workflow-md.mdx`, `configuration/workflow-templates.mdx`, `providers/anthropic.mdx`, `providers/aws-bedrock.mdx`, and `setup/target-repo.mdx` described a structured "Implemented / Gaps / Manual Steps" PR comment from a cheaper model (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), overridable via `gap_analysis_model:`.
- **Source**: No trace of that comment format or the haiku default exists in source. The real feature is `post-push-review` (`ai-implement/src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts:646-999`) — an iterative merge-readiness review on the same model as implementation, posting "Approved" / "Reached review cap" comments. `gap_analysis_model` is accepted (`ai-implement/src/workflow-md.ts:6,14`) but consumed nowhere.
- **Edit**: Rewrote `reference/gap-analysis.mdx` to describe the real review mechanism, removed the dead `gap_analysis_model` accordion/example and cost claims across all listed pages, and replaced "gap analysis comment" language with accurate review-comment language throughout.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in both runs.

### H-3: Six target-repo variables undocumented as legacy-`comment-trigger.yml`-only  (2/2 runs)
- **Docs**: `AI_IMPLEMENT_PROVIDER`, `AI_IMPLEMENT_AWS_REGION`, `AI_IMPLEMENT_MAX_TURNS`, `AI_IMPLEMENT_MAX_ITERATIONS`, `AI_IMPLEMENT_MAX_JOB_MINUTES`, `AI_IMPLEMENT_SKILLS_REPO` were documented as generally effective for `/ai-implement` comment-triggered runs, with no caveat.
- **Source**: All six are read exclusively by `comment-trigger.yml` (`ai-implement/src/workflow-sync.ts:14-31`), which "Sync workflows" removes from every repo it touches; a synced repo's comment-triggered runs pull the equivalents from the project mapping instead (`ai-implement/src/comment-gapfill-drain.ts:267`).
- **Edit**: Added warnings/notes across `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` and `reference/troubleshooting.mdx` stating these variables apply only to repos that haven't re-synced; post-sync, the equivalents live on the project's admin-UI mapping.
- **Priority resolution**: Kept HIGH per the no-downgrade rule; Run 1 rated this MEDIUM.

### H-4: Admin API reference wrongly claims all non-`/api/auth` routes require a bearer token  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx` stated `/api/auth` is the only endpoint that skips bearer-token auth and that every other `/api/*` route returns `401` without one.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/src/index.ts:2336-2364` registers `POST /api/token`, `POST /api/status`, and `POST /api/step-report` — all handled and returned before the generic bearer-auth branch at `index.ts:2543` — so none requires a bearer token. They authenticate via a per-machine nonce instead (`ai-implement/src/run-autonomous.ts:372-374`).
- **Edit**: Narrowed the `/api/auth` claim to "operator-facing" routes and added a new **Session-machine endpoints** subsection documenting the three routes and their nonce-based auth.

### H-5: `RUNNER_MODE` omits that it overrides the admin UI's live toggle  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Described purely as a deploy-time variable.
- **Source**: The Reaper page has a competing DB-backed toggle (`ai-implement/src/admin-ui/pages/reaper.ts:18`) that the source itself warns is inert whenever `RUNNER_MODE` is set (`ai-implement/src/runner-mode.ts:38-52`).
- **Edit**: Added a note cross-referencing the admin-UI toggle and the precedence rule.

### H-6: `FLY_APP_NAME` mischaracterized as "logging only"  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said it's read for logging only.
- **Source**: It tags every session machine this instance creates; the reaper and startup cleanup (`ai-implement/src/fly-machines.ts:388,445`, `reaper.ts:151`) use the tag to avoid destroying another tenant's machines in a shared sessions app.
- **Edit**: Replaced the description with the actual multi-tenant safety role.

### H-7: `push` step's skip condition described backwards  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said push is skipped when `feedback-loop` didn't approve.
- **Source**: Push always runs on a fresh run (opening a normal or draft PR); it's skipped only on gap-fill re-runs (`ai-implement/src/pipeline/pipeline-loader.ts:161-163`).
- **Edit**: Corrected the accordion to describe the draft-PR behavior and the real skip condition.

### H-8: `preflight` mischaracterized as a pre-implementation check  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Described as validating the workspace before Claude starts.
- **Source**: Runs the repo's typecheck/lint/test scripts against Claude's finished, approved diff, right before push (`ai-implement/src/pipeline/steps/preflight.ts:1-83`); a failure doesn't block push.
- **Edit**: Corrected timing, purpose, and non-blocking behavior.

### H-9: `runner-image.mdx` names deprecated `SESSION_IMAGE` instead of current variable  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Resolution-order step 1 cited the orchestrator's "own `SESSION_IMAGE`."
- **Source**: `AI_IMPLEMENT_RUNNER_IMAGE` is the current name (`ai-implement/src/repo-image.ts:150-165`); `SESSION_IMAGE` is a deprecated fallback.
- **Edit**: Updated the resolution-order text.

### H-10: `runner-image.mdx` overstates automatic fallback for an unreachable image  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said an unreachable image falls back automatically.
- **Source**: Only file-shape/format validation triggers fallback (`ai-implement/src/repo-image.ts:61-119`); an unreachable-but-well-formed image fails later at machine-create time.
- **Edit**: Clarified what the automatic check actually covers.

### H-11: `packageManager` invalid values silently fall back instead of failing the run  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said any value outside `npm`/`yarn`/`pnpm` fails the run.
- **Source**: Falls through silently to `npm ci` — no validation rejects a typo (`ai-implement/src/pipeline/steps/install.ts:82-89`).
- **Edit**: Corrected the behavior description.

### H-12: `custom/providers/` is already wired; docs say it isn't  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said the directory is reserved and not wired to a stable interface, with a warning against production use.
- **Source**: `resolveProvider` (`ai-implement/src/providers/index.ts:28-38`) already loads and uses a custom provider factory with the same override precedence as `custom/steps/`.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the section to describe the working mechanism, narrowing the warning to interface-shape stability.

### H-13: Pipeline YAML `inputs:` key is silently dropped, undocumented  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said YAML "only needs" `id`/`type`/`moduleId` without stating what happens to other keys.
- **Source**: Any other key, including `inputs:`, is parsed then discarded (`ai-implement/src/pipeline/pipeline-loader.ts:50-71`); a new custom step always gets an empty `inputs` object.
- **Edit**: Added this to the existing tip.

### H-14: `workflow-md.mdx` `verify` accordion misstates its gate and PR-timing  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said verify runs whenever Claude completes without error, before the PR opens.
- **Source**: Gated on `feedback-loop.approved`, not mere lack of error (`ai-implement/src/pipeline/pipeline-loader.ts:191-202`); an unapproved run still opens a draft PR with verify skipped entirely.
- **Edit**: Corrected the gate and PR-timing description.

### H-15: New-project stepper's Capacity step doesn't expose the run-cap fields  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Both an info box and a full table claimed the stepper's Capacity step exposes `maxTurns`/`maxIterations`/`maxJobMinutes`. `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx` already correctly said these are Edit-dialog-only, directly contradicting `admin-ui.mdx`.
- **Source**: `stepper.ts:210-225`'s Capacity step only renders the max-parallel-issues field; the three caps live only in `projects.ts:134-136`'s Edit dialog.
- **Edit**: Removed the incorrect claims and pointed to the Edit dialog and the accurate page instead.

### H-16: Ticket links hard-coded to Linear across 4 admin panels  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Implied provider-aware ticket links on Sessions, Blockers, and Pull requests panels.
- **Source**: All four link-building call sites (`ai-implement/src/admin-ui/pages/{sessions,blockers,pulls,issues}.ts`) hard-code `linear.app` regardless of the mapping's ticketing provider.
- **Edit**: Added a note on the Pull requests panel (first occurrence) calling out the Linear-only behavior and its effect on Jira-mapped rows, referenced from the other panels.

### H-17: Jira `ticketingConfig` missing the third override field, `profilesFieldOverride`  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: JSON example and prose showed only `statusFieldOverride`/`repoFieldOverride`, calling them "the two" override fields.
- **Source**: A third, `profilesFieldOverride` (`ai-implement/src/providers/ticketing-config.ts:16-18`, `jira.ts:196`), is genuinely consumed to resolve the "AI-Implement Profiles" custom field.
- **Edit**: Added the field to the example and prose, with its consequence when left unset on an ambiguous field name.

### H-18: `labels.mdx` wrongly claims Jira has no blocking semantics  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said Jira has no built-in blocking, unlike Linear.
- **Source**: An open "Blocks"-type issue link filters an issue out of the poll, mirroring Linear's behavior (`ai-implement/src/providers/jira.ts:142-150,252-256`).
- **Edit**: Corrected the warning to describe the actual block-and-clear behavior and its default-link-type limitation.

### H-19: Concurrency section undercounts which states occupy a capacity slot  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Named only the implementation-phase marker (`AI-Working`/`Implementing`) as counting against the cap.
- **Source**: Planning-phase markers (`AI-Planning`/`Planning`) count too (`ai-implement/src/providers/linear.ts:276-280`, `jira.ts:280-282`).
- **Edit**: Updated the sentence to cover the full in-pipeline window.

### H-20: Feature-branch grouping overclaims unlimited nesting depth (actual cap: 5)  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Said the structure "nests as deeply as your issue tree does."
- **Source**: Both providers cap ancestor-chain resolution at 5 levels (`ai-implement/src/providers/linear.ts:182-210`, `jira.ts:389`); a deeper child silently targets the default branch instead.
- **Edit**: Stated the 5-level cap and its effect.

### H-21: `aws-bedrock.mdx` invents a second STS credential exchange for "gap analysis"  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Claimed the credential exchange runs twice per run — once for implementation, once for "gap analysis."
- **Source**: Both workflow files (`ai-implement/workflows/claude-implement.yml:205-211`, `claude-plan.yml:179-185`) call `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` exactly once, requesting a 4-hour session that covers the whole containerized run.
- **Edit**: Corrected the description to one exchange with a 4-hour session, and fixed the related comment-triggered-run and per-step-model claims on the same page.

### H-22: `error-codes.mdx` max-turns example describes a hard failure; actual outcome is graceful  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: Showed a raw `LLM invocation failed with exit code 1` example for hitting the turn cap.
- **Source**: Hitting the cap is explicitly excluded from invocation-error handling (`ai-implement/src/pipeline/steps/implement.ts:74-77`); it ends with a draft PR and a run-autopsy ticket comment instead (`run-autopsy.ts:19-46`).
- **Edit**: Replaced the example and description with the actual draft-PR/run-autopsy outcome.

### H-23: `bd-smoke-jumper` falsely lumped in with "no tracker dependency"  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: A note said the skills not named earlier (`bd-smoke-jumper`, `bd-belay-on`) "don't depend on" a tracker.
- **Source**: `bd-smoke-jumper` (`skills-source/plugin/skills/bd-smoke-jumper/SKILL.md:33,50`) lists tracker MCP as required, reads issue context, and always files failures to the tracker.
- **Edit**: Split the note so only `bd-belay-on` is described as tracker-independent.

## MEDIUM-priority finding details

### M-1: `ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE` unset returns 503, not 404  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` says unset means `/admin` and `/api/` routes "return 404."
- **Source**: `index.ts:2544-2549` returns 503 with an explanatory JSON error; 404 only applies to genuinely unmatched routes.

### M-2: `REAPER_ALERT_THRESHOLD` `ParamField` missing its actual default  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: No `default` prop set.
- **Source**: Defaults to `10` (`index.ts:172`, `.env.example`).

### M-3: `verify` skip condition diverges from push's own skip flag  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: `customize/custom-steps.mdx` says verify is skipped "when push was skipped."
- **Source**: Verify's actual skip check is `feedback-loop.approved`, which diverges from push's own `Boolean(ctx.data.prNumber)` check on an approved gap-fill run (`pipeline-loader.ts:191-201`).

### M-4: Bedrock "hard-fails with a clear error" claim unconfirmed  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: `customize/workflow-md.mdx` and `providers/aws-bedrock.mdx` claim an explicit hard-fail guard when `model:` is omitted on a Bedrock-mapped repo.
- **Source**: No such guard found in `run-autonomous.ts`, the pipeline executor, or the workflow YAMLs; model resolution falls back to a default regardless of provider. Flagged at reduced confidence since a guard elsewhere can't be fully ruled out.

### M-5: Reaper page's runner-mode toggle has 4 buttons; docs list 5 valid modes  (1/2 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx` lists `default`/`gha`/`fly`/`local`/`shadow` as toggle options.

## Synthesis decisions log (audit-trail for reviewers)

### H-1
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH, Run 2 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** Run 1's H-1 ("`/ai-implement` PR comments are handled by the orchestrator webhook, not `comment-trigger.yml`") and Run 2's H-1 (`GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` consequence text) + H-21 (comment-trigger.yml removal) all cite the same underlying behavior — `workflow-sync.ts` removes `comment-trigger.yml` on sync, and `webhook.ts` handles `/ai-implement` directly with no polling fallback. Folded into one finding.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 2 for 9 of 11 files; Run 1 for the admin-ui.mdx Bedrock-warning caveat and status-code fix (folded into H-4's file, see below); merged Run 1 content into `quickstart.mdx` and `reference/gap-analysis.mdx`.
- **Selection reasoning:** On every file both runs edited for this finding (`setup/github-app.mdx`, `setup/target-repo.mdx`, `reference/troubleshooting.mdx`, `configuration/workflow-templates.mdx`, `configuration/environment-variables.mdx`, `providers/aws-bedrock.mdx`, `reference/labels.mdx`, `how-it-works.mdx`), Run 2's edit was a strict superset of Run 1's — it additionally distinguishes legacy (pre-sync) repos from synced (envelope) repos, a distinction Run 1's edits omit. Two exceptions required merging Run 1's unique content into Run 2's base: `quickstart.mdx` (Run 1 added a webhook cross-reference sentence Run 2's edit lacked) and `reference/gap-analysis.mdx` (Run 1 added a webhook-required `<Info>` callout that Run 2's full-page rewrite, done for H-2, didn't carry over).

**Edit candidates compared:**

Run 1's approach to `setup/github-app.mdx` (not selected):
```mdx
- **`/ai-implement` comments.** The orchestrator receives the comment through this
  webhook, checks the commenter has write access, and dispatches a gap-fill run.
  Without an active webhook, `/ai-implement` comments have no effect.
```

Run 2's approach to `setup/github-app.mdx` (selected):
```mdx
But skipping it disables two things with no fallback: **automatic follow-up runs
on review feedback** ..., and the **`/ai-implement` comment trigger itself** on
repos synced to the current workflow generation — the orchestrator's webhook is
the only thing that listens for that comment on such a repo, so without it,
commenting `/ai-implement` does nothing.
```

### H-2
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH, Run 2 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** Run 1's H-3 ("Anthropic provider page states a false gap-analysis model default") and Run 2's H-6 ("the 'gap analysis' PR-comment feature doesn't exist") cite the identical source evidence (`post-push-review.ts:646-999` resolving the review model, `workflow-md.ts:6,14` showing `gap_analysis_model` is parsed but never consumed) and target overlapping docs surface (`providers/anthropic.mdx`). Run 2's finding is the root-cause framing — the whole "gap analysis" feature as documented doesn't exist, of which the false model default is one symptom — so folded together.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 2, for all 12 files.
- **Selection reasoning:** Run 1's edit only fixed the false default sentence and left the fabricated "Implemented / Gaps / Manual Steps" comment format and `gap_analysis_model` example block intact on `reference/gap-analysis.mdx` and other pages. Run 2's edit rewrote the feature description at its root (real mechanism: `post-push-review`, iterative approve/re-review loop) and propagated the correction consistently across every affected page, which is strictly more complete and avoids leaving a partially-corrected, still-misleading feature description in place.

### H-3
- **Present in:** Run 1 MEDIUM, Run 2 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** Run 1's M-1 ("Several pages still describe `/ai-implement` repo variables as universally applicable") and Run 2's H-2 ("Six target-repo variables undocumented as legacy-only") describe the identical drift — the same six `AI_IMPLEMENT_*` repo variables are read only by the removed `comment-trigger.yml`, so post-sync they silently do nothing.
- **Priority resolution:** Kept HIGH per the no-downgrade rule; Run 1 rated this MEDIUM and left it report-only.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 2 (Run 1 produced no edit for this finding, having rated it MEDIUM).
- **Selection reasoning:** Only one candidate edit existed since Run 1 didn't produce one at this tier.
